jobs.occupation: Post-Doc: Agentic AI for Self-Driving Labs in Materials Science (Ingenieur/in - Materialwissenschaften)
jobs.description: Self-driving laboratories are revolutionizing material science these days. They rely on autonomous robotic systems that can massively speed up experimental work. Agentic Artificial Intelligence (Al) is controlling them, for example, by analyzing the data they collect and planning new experiments based on these data.At the Hereon Institute of Surface Science, we study how light metals degrade and how to control that degradation for structural, biomedical and energy storage applications. Our robotic testing platform already screens hundreds of electrolyte additives and will be extended to screen coating formulations, generating data for machine learning. In this project, in strong collaboration with the Hereon Institute of Material System Modeling you will build the AI agents that will screen properties of chemical compounds, design experiments, analyze results in real time, and draw on the literature and on our growing databases to decide what to try next. You will work hand in hand with experimental researchers, focused on degradation control. Their laboratories will be the proving ground for your agents. Join us to build a self-driving laboratory of corrosion science.We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a Postdoc in the quickly developing field of agentic AI for materials science. The position is full-time (39 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg).Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position.Your tasks:- design and implement AI agents that plan, execute and evaluate experiments on our robotic testing platform- integrate the agents with our laboratory equipment and IT infrastructure, including electronic lab notebooks and databases, to enable closed-loop experimentation- develop decision-making strategies that combine large language models (LLMs) with active learning and Bayesian optimization, so that promising compounds, coating formulations and testing conditions are identified with as few experiments as possible- work side by side with experimental scientists and translate their scientific questions into autonomous workflows that accelerate their research- build tools that extract knowledge from scientific literature and from our own datasets, turning them into machine-readable, FAIR resources- publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports and contribute to open-source software and open datasetsYour profile:- a completed Master's and PhD degree in computational materials science, computational engineering, computer science, data science, chemistry, physics or a related field- strong programming skills in Python and hands-on experience with large language models (LLMs), agent frameworks, or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)- experience with machine learning (ideally also active learning or Bayesian optimization)- experience with robotics, instrument control, APls, databases or software engineering- genuine interest in laboratory automation and in applying AI to real scientific problems- basic knowledge of chemistry, electrochemistry and materials science- enjoying teamwork and clear communication across disciplines, particularly with experimental researchers- very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learningOur jobs.description: LocationDuisburgApplication areaFaculty of Physics, Theoretical PhysicsDoctoral Researcher at the interface of theoretical physics and computational materials science (f/m/d)TV-L 13 (gross 44.493 € - 63.239 €)We are looking for a curious and motivated PhD candidate to join our newly established research group at the interface of theoretical physics and computational materials science. The project explores how interactions between electrons and atomic magnetic moments give rise to the collective behaviour of magnetic materials. A central research direction is to understand and design materials that support topological spin textures such as skyrmions and hopfions and investigate their potential for brain-inspired, or neuromorphic, computing.Start of employment2027-03-01Duration of employment3.5 yearsWorking time29 h 52 min (75%)Your main tasksYou will carry out high-throughput simulations: automated sets of calculations across selected materials and magnetic configurations. Using density functional theory (DFT), with established software such as VASP and FLEUR, you will investigate electronic structure and determine the magnetic interactions that govern how atomic moments arrange themselves and evolve. Particular attention will be paid to materials in which relativistic effects and competing magnetic interactions favour complex spin textures. Relevant material families include two-dimensional magnets, rare-earth intermetallics and magnetic Weyl semimetals.A key question is how quantum calculations can be translated into reliable spin models that predict the stability and dynamics of topological spin textures. You will combine physical modelling with physics-constrained machine learning, including symbolic regression, to develop spin Hamiltonians describing interactions between atomic magnetic moments. These will underpin atomistic simulations within an automated workflow for identifying promising materials and investigating how composition, doping or strain can tune their magnetic behaviour.The duties include teaching obligations amounting to 3 hours per week.You will be given the opportunity to pursue further academic qualification as part of this role.Your profile- a Master’s degree in
